**BCG odds ratio = 1.107 (95% CI 0.803–1.526, p = 0.536)** — from a proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression (statsmodels `OrderedModel`, logit link, n=1000) of the 5-level COVID-19 severity outcome (0=no COVID-19 AE; 1=Mild; 2=Moderate; 3=Severe; 4=Critical/death, subject worst-event) on BCG vaccination (vs placebo), prior medical-history count (present MH conditions at screening), patient interaction frequency (`patients_seen` scored 1/2/3), plus the three pairwise two-way interactions (BCG×hist, BCG×freq, hist×freq); covariates mean-centered, OR read at mean history count (1.03) and mean frequency (1.20).

**Interpretation:** BCG vaccination was not significantly associated with COVID-19 severity — the OR is close to 1 and its CI spans 1, so no protective (or harmful) effect is detected in this trial. The BCG estimate tilts upwards at low contact (OR=1.18 at patients_seen 1–50) and downwards at high contact (OR=0.63 at >100) but the BCG×frequency interaction is non-significant (p≈0.31). By contrast, higher interaction frequency (OR=1.90/score unit, p=0.002) and more prior conditions (OR=1.22, p=0.034) each predict higher severity.

**Key assumption:** severity is constructed from AE `AESEV` (worst COVID event per subject; the 43 infected subjects with missing AESEV — all non-serious — were imputed to Mild). Sensitivity analyses were consistent: AEHS 9-level outcome OR=1.13 (0.82–1.55); expect_interact proxy OR=1.06 (0.77–1.46); work_hours proxy OR=1.07 (0.78–1.47); dropping hist×freq OR=1.11 (0.81–1.54); main-effects-only OR=1.10 (0.81–1.51). Proportional-odds verification was strained only at the sparse top cut (>3, 18 events).
